title: Choose and work with a manufacturing partner
summary: Most hardware teams use a contract manufacturer. Choose one that fits your volume and product, and treat them as part of the team.

beginner: Learn what a contract manufacturer does: buys parts, assembles, tests and ships.
List what you need: volume, product type, certifications and location.
Shortlist three manufacturers, ideally through referrals.
Send each the same request for a quote and compare more than price.
Visit or video-tour the shortlisted factories before you sign.
intermediate: Match your volume to a partner where you are a meaningful customer.
Agree quality checks, change control and who orders parts.
Hold a regular call on cost, quality and lead times.
experienced: Set a manufacturing strategy across products, including a second partner.
Negotiate contracts that cover intellectual property and capacity.
Measure partners on quality, cost and delivery each quarter.

canDelegateTo.task: Review the contract and IP terms

toolExamples.confluence: Keep a scorecard for each manufacturer on one page.
toolExamples.notion: Track quotes and visit notes in one database.

definitionOfDone: Partner chosen with quality and change-control terms agreed
pitfalls: Being too small a customer to get attention
